cross_schema_coupling.independent: one selector per item/group; with probability 0.0 both schemas use the same latent draw, otherwise each schema uses its own independent draw
cross_schema_coupling.partial: one selector per item/group; with probability 0.5 both schemas use the same latent draw, otherwise each schema uses its own independent draw
cross_schema_coupling.shared: one selector per item/group; with probability 1.0 both schemas use the same latent draw, otherwise each schema uses its own independent draw

assumptions.effect: equal target effect in both schemas
assumptions.equal_effect_limitation: because the true effect is equal in both schemas, simulated sign flips are near zero; Phase 3A OBSERVED sign flips between schemas (schema-dependent effects), which this simulation does not model and which would lower power further
assumptions.exact_method: paired cluster-bootstrap percentile 95% interval, 2000 resamples (the planned gate uses 10,000; percentile resolution differs slightly); now also run at partial coupling
assumptions.interpretation: group counts are planning ranges for this synthetic distribution, not guaranteed repository sample sizes; real power is expected to be lower
not_modelled: training-seed variance (no permitted evidence; NOT estimated)
repository-native outcome variance (no repository-native outcome data exists yet; unavailable)
more than two fixed inputs per function
assumptions.outcome_source: synthetic train-side MBPP simple/moderate Phase 3A outcomes (240 semantic groups, 2 items each), NOT repository-native outcomes

rules.confirmatory_5: lower 95% bound > +5 under both schemas, no sign flip
rules.positive_both: lower 95% bound > 0 under both schemas, no sign flip
rules.sign_flip: point estimates of opposite sign across the two schemas

assumptions.treatment_template: arm A 431 outcomes on the same items, shifted to each target effect by flipping outcomes

interpretation: group counts are planning ranges for this synthetic train-side distribution, not guaranteed repository sample sizes; training-seed variance and repository-native variance are unmodelled and the answer-rate, validity and diversity gates are outside the power calculation, so real power is expected to be lower

scientific_gates.exceeds_five_points: lower 95% bound > +5 under both schemas with no sign flip: evidence that the effect EXCEEDS five points
scientific_gates.positive_effect: lower 95% bound > 0 under both schemas with no sign flip: evidence that the effect is POSITIVE; says nothing about its size
scientific_gates.reconciliation: the two gates answer different questions and have very different power. A true 5-point effect can never be shown to exceed 5 points (its lower bound sits below 5 by construction); a true 10-point effect needs several hundred groups for that gate. Around 200-350 groups the design is an EXPLORATORY POSITIVE-EFFECT SCREEN: it does NOT confirm a five-point effect unless the true effect is substantially larger (about 10 points or more)

status: PLANNING EVIDENCE, NOT A POWER GUARANTEE

supersedes.reason: v1 drew an independent shared/not-shared selector per schema, so its declared partial coupling c=0.5 was an effective shared-draw probability of c**2=0.25; v2 uses one common selector per item or semantic group
